response.sql:
WITH album_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    SUM(CASE WHEN Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN Bytes ELSE 0 END) as total_bytes,
    SUM(CASE WHEN Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN Milliseconds ELSE 0 END) as total_milliseconds,
    COUNT(*) as track_count
  FROM Track
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
album_rates AS (
  SELECT 
    CAST(total_bytes AS DECIMAL) / CAST(total_milliseconds AS DECIMAL) as rate,
    track_count
  FROM album_stats
  WHERE total_bytes > 0 AND total_milliseconds > 0
),
mean_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) as mean_rate
  FROM album_rates
),
filtered_above_mean AS (
  SELECT 
    ar.rate,
    ar.track_count,
    (ar.rate - mr.mean_rate) as excess
  FROM album_rates ar
  CROSS JOIN mean_rate mr
  WHERE ar.rate > mr.mean_rate
)
SELECT 
  AVG(rate) as avg_rate,
  AVG(track_count) as avg_track_count,
  AVG(excess) as avg_excess
FROM filtered_above_mean;

assumptions.assumption: Track count for each album includes all tracks in that album (including those with NULL Bytes). The 'ignoring missing sizes' phrase applies only to the rate calculation, not to track enumeration.

alternatives.interpretation: Track count refers only to tracks with available size information (non-NULL Bytes), so an album with 5 total tracks but only 3 with bytes would have track_count=3.
